a: Kafka is a distributed log for high-throughput event streaming.
A topic is a named stream of records partitioned across brokers.
Consumer groups share work so each partition is consumed by one member.
RabbitMQ is a message broker supporting queues, exchanges, and routing keys.
Pub/sub publishes events to many subscribers without tight coupling.
At-least-once may duplicate messages; consumers must be idempotent.
Exactly-once is hard; systems approximate it with transactions and idempotency.
A DLQ holds messages that failed processing after retries.
Ordering is usually guaranteed per partition/queue key, not globally.
Stream processing computes continuously on unbounded event streams.
Offsets track a consumer's position in a partition.
Evolve event schemas carefully (backward/forward compatible) with registries.
